sources.licence: No open licence. North Ground records facts — dates, units, classes and limits — with the printed cell as provenance.

conditions.text: A Wildlife Identification Number, a wildlife certificate and a licence for this species are required. North Ground has not verified what you hold.

This season applies only to hunters with an applicable special licence from the Alberta Hunting Draws. The answer assumes you hold one valid for this species, class and unit; North Ground has not verified it.
Hunting with a bow and arrow also requires a bowhunting permit (not required for a crossbow).
Licences open to non-residents differ from residents', and non-residents hunt big game with a resident hunter host or a designated guide.
Hunting big game on Sundays is unlawful in WMUs 102–160, 624, 728, 730 and 936; Sundays are excluded from the dates given here.
Heads of deer harvested in specific WMUs must be submitted for chronic wasting disease testing.
Hunters, including bowhunters, require a firearms discharge permit to hunt in WMU 936 (Cooking Lake–Blackfoot Provincial Recreation Area).
A wildlife certificate and an Alberta game bird licence are required. North Ground has not verified what you hold.
WMUs 728 and 730 (CFB Wainwright): every hunter attends a mandatory 7:00 am safety briefing on their first day, and game-bird hunters using shotguns must use non-toxic shot.

Hunting big game with a rifle or shotgun is unlawful in WMUs 212, 247, 248 and 410; a general season there is open to a muzzleloader, crossbow or bow unless the guide states otherwise for that season.
conditions.sourceSection: General Regulations, Big game — It is unlawful to set out, use or employ a rifle or shotgun in WMUs 212, 247, 248 or 410

conditions.text: This season is open only to hunting with a bow, crossbow, muzzleloader or shotgun.

A 3-point or larger elk is a male elk with an antler whose main beam carries at least two tines, each at least 7.6 cm (3 in.) long, with the tip of the main beam at least 7.6 cm (3 in.) beyond the base of the last tine counted.
conditions.sourceSection: Big Game Regulations, Big Game Identification — Three-point elk

conditions.text: A 6-point or larger elk is a male elk with an antler whose main beam carries at least five tines, each at least 7.6 cm (3 in.) long, with the tip of the main beam at least 7.6 cm (3 in.) beyond the base of the last tine counted.
conditions.sourceSection: Big Game Regulations, Big Game Identification — Six-point elk

conditions.text: This season is for a calf moose only, under a calf moose special licence. The guide describes a calf as small, with a short nose and face, about 1.2 m (4 ft.) high at the shoulder, and seldom alone.
conditions.sourceSection: Big Game Regulations, Big Game Identification — Moose; Evidence of sex, species and class

conditions.text: In WMU 353 the special-licence season for antlerless moose applies only to part of the unit, set out in the Alberta Hunting Draws booklet.

In this WMU the special-licence (draw) season for antlerless elk applies only to part of the unit, set out in the Alberta Hunting Draws booklet; an archery season for antlerless elk there covers the whole unit.
conditions.sourceSection: p. 53, Foothills footnote 1; p. 55, Mountain footnote 2

conditions.text: In WMU 624 this elk season is open Monday to Friday only; Saturdays and Sundays are excluded from the dates given here.
conditions.sourceSection: p. 47, Prairie WMUs (WMU 624 - Monday to Friday only)

conditions.text: It is unlawful to hunt a black bear under one year old, or a female black bear accompanied by a cub under one year old.

limitations: Alberta's own catalogue record says the guide "is neither a legal document nor a complete listing of current Alberta hunting regulations"; the Wildlife Act and the Wildlife Regulation (Alta. Reg. 143/97) are the law.
Alberta describes its WMU maps as small-scale approximations of units legally described in the Wildlife Regulation, which prevails near a boundary.
Being inside a WMU is not permission to hunt there: land access, provincial parks, restricted areas and local bylaws are separate questions North Ground has not resolved.
This is a recreational licence result. It is not a determination of treaty, Aboriginal or Métis harvesting rights.

blackBearSpring2027.reason: Printed as "Spring 2027 (Requires a new year licence)": a season of the next licence year, outside the period this bundle certifies.

notEncoded.additionalDrawHunts: Alberta's additional special-licence draw hunts (class 2 sheep, CFB Wainwright deer and moose, pronghorn, either-sex elk in WMUs 728 and 730, mountain goat) are not encoded; their units are not named for those species in the region tables, so they answer UNKNOWN. The WMU 300 3-point elk hunt is carried as unsettled days.

criterion.statedAs: Antlered - A white-tailed deer, moose or elk having an antler exceeding 10.2 cm (4 in.) in length.
criterion.sourceSection: Big Game Regulations, Big Game Identification

legalAnimalClasses.criterionBlocker: The guide's definition of antlered names white-tailed deer, moose and elk, not mule deer; the Wildlife Regulation's own definition for mule deer has not been read.
The guide's definition of antlerless names white-tailed deer, moose and elk, not mule deer; the Wildlife Regulation's own definition for mule deer has not been read.

Alberta's test is compound — at least two tines on the main beam, each at least 7.6 cm (3 in.), with the beam tip at least 7.6 cm beyond the last tine counted — and the criterion model holds one measure. The full definition is carried as condition ab-elk-three-point.

Alberta's test is compound — at least five tines on the main beam, each at least 7.6 cm (3 in.), with the beam tip at least 7.6 cm beyond the last tine counted — and the criterion model holds one measure. The full definition is carried as condition ab-elk-six-point.
